question: In a chemical reaction, a substance gains hydrogen. This process is said to be ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**reduction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reduction:**

 
 
• Reduction is a chemical reaction where a substance gains electrons. 
 
• This gain of electrons leads to a decrease in the oxidation state of the substance. 
 
• A classic example is the reduction of iron ore (Fe2O3) to iron metal (Fe) in a blast furnace. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation:**

 
 
• Oxidation is the opposite of reduction. 
 
• It involves the loss of electrons by a substance. 
 
• This loss of electrons results in an increase in the oxidation state of the substance. 
 
• A common example is the rusting of iron, where iron metal (Fe) reacts with oxygen (O2) to form iron oxide (Fe2O3), which is rust. 
 
 
 
• **Chlorination:**
 
 
• Chlorination is a chemical reaction where chlorine (Cl2) is added to a substance. 
 
• It often involves the substitution of hydrogen atoms with chlorine atoms. 
 
• Chlorination is used to purify water by killing harmful bacteria and is also used in the production of various chemicals. 
 
 
 
• **Bromination:**
 
 
• Bromination is a chemical reaction where bromine (Br2) is added to a substance. 
 
• Similar to chlorination, it often involves the substitution of hydrogen atoms with bromine atoms. 
 
• Bromination is used in the production of various organic compounds and in some industrial processes.
